newsitem.title: USA: BP to restore crude, natgas US Gulf output.
newsitem.headline: BP to restore crude, natgas US Gulf output.

text.p: British Petroleum said Tuesday it was in the process of restoring crude and natural gas production cut at three offshore oil platforms in the U.S. Gulf Coast due to Tropical Storm Josephine yesterday.
"Workers started returning to all our facilities this morning. Over the next day or so, production will be back up to normal," Hugh Depland, spokesman for BP Exploration said.
A total of 67,000 barrels per day (bpd) of gross crude oil and 64 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gross natural gas were reduced from three out of four fields operated by BP.
BP operates about 70,000 bpd of gross crude and 72 million mmcfd of gross natural gas in the U.S. Gulf.
The three platforms shut-in since Sunday afternoon were Pompano, Amberjack and Ewing Bank 826.
